subject.title: fix(agents): strip MiniMax stream-boundary marker from transport payload text (#104403)

question: Should the marker cleanup be accepted only as a MiniMax/minimax-portal provider-stream behavior, rather than as a global `sanitizeTransportPayloadText` rule?
rationale: The shared helper has no provider identity, while the alternative changes stream-finalization semantics and is already being explored in a related provider-scoped PR; selecting the permanent owner boundary is a maintainer product and architecture choice.

options.title: Use the provider hook
options.body: Move the cleanup into the MiniMax/minimax-portal stream wrapper and retain a terminal candidate until `done` or `error`, with literal-content preservation coverage.

options.title: Approve global sanitization
options.body: Accept the cross-provider text-removal risk only if maintainers explicitly define these marker fragments as universally invalid transport payload bytes.

options.title: Consolidate on the related PR
options.body: Choose the provider-scoped work in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/105243 as the implementation vehicle after it is rebased, made mergeable, and receives sufficient real proof.

recommendation.title: Use the provider hook
recommendation.body: Move the cleanup into the MiniMax/minimax-portal stream wrapper and retain a terminal candidate until `done` or `error`, with literal-content preservation coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: Their related provider-stream implementation is the closest available evidence-backed owner candidate for the boundary decision.
